title: Task Implementer Output Contract
description: JSON result task-implementer writes in Phase 6.1. Registered as contract `task-implementer-output`: validate a result with `keryx skills contracts validate <result.json> --schema task-implementer-output`.

status.description: success: all criteria met, all verifications pass; partial: some criteria met or verification failures; failed: critical blockers

test_result.description: pass OR 'N passed, M failed: <details>' OR 'skipped'

acceptance_criteria_met.description: all OR 'partial: <list of unmet criteria>' OR none

skill_drift.description: Set from SKILL.md Phase 2.0b: 'none' | 'stale: <module>/<skill> — <what diverged>' | 'missing: <module> should have a project-skill'. SKILL.md has required this field since project-skill verification was added; this object is `additionalProperties: false`, so until it was declared here a compliant result was REFUSED by its own contract.

noticed_not_touched.description: Problems seen in passing and deliberately left alone because they were out of scope. Candidate follow-up work: the location is required because a note a reader has to go searching for is a note nobody acts on. Omit the field when nothing was noticed; `[]` says the same thing explicitly.

what.description: The problem, stated so a follow-up task could be written from it alone

where.description: Path, directory or symbol it lives at

assumptions.description: What was assumed where the task did not say. A wrong assumption is the usual cause of a rejected result, so these are the first thing a reviewer should check. Read only by a human — nothing in the result or the request can confirm an assumption, so this is deliberately an array of sentences rather than a structure that would imply a check nobody performs.

behavior_changes.description: Behavior the implementer chose where the task and the plan's state × event matrix did not decide it. Every user-visible tradeoff (message wording, error placement, which state resets or survives) is listed with `user_visible: true, needs_operator: true`; flow-orchestrator Phase 2 asks the operator before accepting a result carrying such an entry, so a tradeoff recorded only in `assumptions` or `notes` is one nobody decided.

description.description: What now behaves differently, stated as the user or caller would observe it

user_visible.description: A user of the product can see the difference

needs_operator.description: The choice is a product decision the operator must confirm before the result is accepted

alternatives.description: The options not taken, so the operator chooses between real alternatives rather than approving the one shown

not_touched.description: Files a reader would expect in `files_modified` and will not find there, each with the reason. `path` is a separate field because this is machine-checkable: a reader holding the request can subtract `files_modified`/`files_created`/`files_deleted` and this list from `task.target_files` and flag whatever is left as an unexplained omission.

reason.description: Why it was left alone — 'already correct', 'out of scope', 'blocked by <x>'

project_context_applied.description: Which of the files `keryx skills resolve-context` listed this run actually used, so a reader can subtract it from the resolver's `must_read` list. `how`: `read` - the file was opened and its text used; `followed` - its rules were applied through a skill or another file that already contains them; `n/a` - the file does not touch the task, with the reason in `notes`. `sha256` is the resolver's value for the file, not a fresh hash: `keryx skills contracts validate --resolved` compares the two.

path.description: Repo-relative path exactly as the resolver printed it

sha256.description: The resolver's sha256 of the file

anchor.description: Optional. The heading of the section read, exactly as the resolver printed it for an entry promoted by a declared condition (flow 462)

summary.description: Optional. What the section says, in the worker's own words; for a promoted entry `keryx skills contracts validate --resolved` checks it against the anchored section (flow 462)

notes.description: Warnings, blockers, or additional context. The three fields above were carved out of this one: free text is where they went before they were declared, and anything that fits one of them belongs there instead.
